ctor.rationale: `base(1, CardType.Skill, CardRarity.Uncommon, TargetType.Self)` (InfernalBlade.cs:15-18) == cost 1 / SKILL / UNCOMMON / SELF.

OnPlay.rationale: RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-04 against current source (file re-shrunk since last audit; only line numbers moved). C# is `CardFactory.GetDistinctForCombat(Owner, characterPool.Where(c => c.Type == Attack), 1, Owner.RunState.Rng.CombatCardGeneration)` then `SetToFreeThisTurn()` then `AddGeneratedCardToCombat(cardModel, PileType.Hand, Owner)` (InfernalBlade.cs:22-29). The sim branches on `crng.is_parity` and calls `get_distinct_for_combat_parity(crng.card_gen, 1, CardType.ATTACK, pool=ctx.combat.card_pool)` (infernal_blade.py:39-43), keeping the shared legacy rng only for non-parity RL runs (44-48) -- the correct-stream pattern; `card/jack_of_all_trades` and `card/jackpot` in this same batch now also route through `combat_rng.card_gen` directly (colorless_skills.py:449, colorless_attacks.py:265), closing the RNG-stream gap those two used to carry (see their own records). The free-this-turn-then-add order matches (infernal_blade.py:50-51), and `set_free_this_turn` is cleared by the turn-end reset `reset_turn_cost_modifiers` (cards/base.py:513-518, was `:265-269`) like C#'s EndOfTurn expiration. The C# filter is the CHARACTER pool restricted to Attacks; `random_pool_cards`/`get_distinct_for_combat_parity` default to the combat's `card_pool` (Ironclad), the same membership.

OnUpgrade.rationale: `EnergyCost.UpgradeBy(-1)` (InfernalBlade.cs:34) == `self._energy_cost -= 1` (1 -> 0). No clamp is needed at this base cost, so the missing `max(0, ...)` other cards use is harmless here.
